payload.friendly_name: Review context carries the WP diff and cited requirement text
payload.purpose_context: Reviewers today get empty or Mission-wide REVIEW COMMANDS on single_branch and only bare requirement IDs, so they spend ~100 git commands hunting the implementation commit and ~100 reads of spec.md. This Mission computes each work package's review range from its recorded window and inlines a bounded diff plus the cited requirement text (issue #7578).
payload.purpose_tldr: The review prompt shows each work package's own diff and the text of the requirements it cites.

options: A (rec): always inline stat + commit list; inline full patch up to a cap (~400 changed lines / 32 KB), else truncate per file with a marker and print the exact git diff command for the remainder
B: never inline patch text; stat + commit list + one exact command only
C: write the full diff to a file beside the review prompt and reference it
payload.question: Q1: How is the inlined WP diff bounded in the review prompt?

options: A (rec): newest for_review lane_head stamp (the snapshot submitted for review); fall back to the commit that introduced that for_review event; note when the live branch has moved past it
B: live branch tip (current behaviour; leaks later commits)
payload.question: Q2: What is the upper bound (tip) of the WP review range?

options: A (rec): read-side only: base = commit that introduced the FR-021 opener event (fallback wp-base ref), tip = commit that introduced the for_review event; no writer change
B: add a new stamp on the write checkout HEAD at claim/for_review (writer change touching ADR 2026-11-08-2 W-1)
payload.question: Q3: On commit-to-target single_branch (no wp_window / lane_head recorded), how is the range anchored?

options: A (rec): yes for the inlined patch and stat on every topology (lane-mates and parallel claims otherwise leak in), but list out-of-map paths touched in the window as a separate warning line so nothing is hidden
B: owned_files scope on repo root only (current behaviour); lane diff unscoped
payload.question: Q4: Scope the review diff to the WP owned_files on lane topologies too?

options: A (rec): tidy-first move of the pure selector (window_opener_events, window_open_of, WindowOpen/WindowGap) to status/wp_window.py, re-exported from consolidation/wp_attribution; behaviour-preserving
B: leave it in consolidation and add a second, review-side selector
payload.question: Q5: Where does the FR-021 window-opener selector live so the review prompt (src/runtime, which may not import consolidation) can reuse it?

options: A (rec): no folds; REFS #3481 #3925 #7120 #7345 #5721; Related (excluded, gate policy / sub-epic E) #6851 #5675 #5331
B: fold #6851 or #5675 (gate-policy change; out of #7578 non-goals)
payload.question: Q6: Fold set for this Mission?

payload.final_answer: A: newest for_review lane_head stamp; fall back to the commit that introduced that for_review event; note when the live branch moved past it
A: scope to owned_files on every topology; list out-of-map paths touched in the window as a separate warning line
A: tidy-first move of the pure FR-021 selector to status/wp_window.py, re-exported from consolidation/wp_attribution
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-11-12 (accepted recommendation); runtime may not import consolidation.

payload.final_answer: Commands only: no inlined patch and no diff file. The prompt carries the WP range base..tip with provenance, the implementation commit list, a compact stat, and the exact git log / git diff commands scoped to owned paths. #7578 Done-when reinterpreted: non-empty, window-limited range + commits + stat with matching commands.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-11-12: the reviewer can fetch the diff with git tooling; the benchmark failure was an empty/unbounded command, not a missing inline diff.

payload.final_answer: Widen the Mission: add the writer stamp (wp_window open_sha and lane_head) for commit-to-target single_branch at the write checkout HEAD, and accept the resulting consolidation-verdict change (check_write_branch_windows reads recorded windows). Requires an amendment to ADR 2026-11-08-2.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-11-12: one canonical window authority on every topology instead of a read-side derivation. Foreign-commit treatment on a shared target is a plan-phase design point to escalate if it changes refusal codes.

options: Narrow: only when the scoped range is unavailable or no owned_files (code/message unchanged)
Keep: whenever the claim commit cannot be found
payload.question: Q7: When does OWNED_REVIEW_BASE_UNAVAILABLE fire once the review range resolves from the recorded window?

payload.final_answer: Narrow: the refusal (code and message unchanged) fires only when the owned checkout's scoped range is unavailable or the WP declares no owned_files; cells pinned on an unresolvable claim commit are re-pinned to genuinely-unavailable fixtures, never deleted.
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-11-12: firing less often is the purpose of the friction reduction; reviews should only be blocked on actual lineage problems.

payload.question: NFR-002 caps the review range at 10 git calls. Since WP02's stamps, a commit-to-target Mission whose events predate the stamps (the DERIVED path) costs a constant 11: read_lane_head now returns the target head, so the moved-past rev-parse + rev-list run. Split the budget (recorded <=10, derived <=12, both constant), or cut a production call (drop the moved-past note on derived ranges / merge a race-guard probe)?

payload.rationale: The derived path now serves only commit-to-target Missions whose events predate the #7578 stamps; its cost stays constant (11, independent of range size), which is NFR-002's intent. Cutting the moved-past note would hide a real fact from the reviewer; merging a race-guard probe weakens a correctness guard. No refusal, exit code, gate severity or ADR behaviour changes, so this is not an operator escalation; flagged in the PR.
